final_recommendation: The room converged on a UBS acquisition with a CHF 50 billion SNB capital floor, to be announced jointly with Banking Act resolution trigger language on Sunday 06:00. UBS board committed by Saturday 13:00; if UBS hesitates Sunday morning, Banking Act resolution fires immediately with no negotiation window.
minority_objections: CS CEO initially pushed for Saturday 22:00 announcement to stop the run earlier, overruled by Federal Council citing deal risk
Wealth client demanded written guarantees by Saturday 04:00, denied as legally infeasible
key_conflicts: Timing of public announcement: CS CEO wanted Saturday evening vs Federal Council insisting on Sunday 06:00 to avoid burning deal if UBS hesitated
Liability allocation: prolonged debate over whether SNB's 50B sits on SNB balance sheet post-close or transfers to UBS as asset
AT1 treatment: conflict over whether to announce AT1 subordination in Saturday statement vs holding until Sunday, resolved by including explicit loss language Saturday 14:15
key_concessions: Federal Council agreed to Saturday 14:15 statement (earlier than planned Sunday 06:00) when deposit outflows hit 6B threshold
SNB committed to 50B facility with hard cap and no clawback/reopener clauses to secure UBS commitment
UBS accepted deal conditional on Federal Council triggering Banking Act resolution at 18:00 Sunday if deal doesn't close
Saturday statement included explicit AT1 subordination language despite risk of accelerating Sunday deposit flight
red_lines: Federal Council: no blank cheque beyond 50B ceiling; taxpayers do not absorb capital losses beyond that floor
UBS: will not sign without written 50B loss cap by Sunday 05:00; no liability beyond that threshold
SNB: will not front-load balance sheet losses beyond emergency liquidity mandate without Federal Council legal cover
Federal Council: if UBS hesitates Sunday 05:00, Banking Act resolution triggers immediately with no extension window
FINMA: no deposit/senior claim guarantees without formal Banking Act resolution framework as legal foundation
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Litigation risk from AT1 holders was raised once by AT1 rep but never developed into concrete legal exposure assessment or mitigation strategy
Second-wave deposit flight risk after AT1 subordination announcement was flagged multiple times but room bet on statement killing the run rather than planning for managed resolution scenario
Market reaction to simultaneous buyer announcement and resolution trigger language—no discussion of how markets would interpret this dual signal
downstream_risk_variables: Sunday morning deposit flows after creditors digest Saturday's AT1 subordination language (5B spike threshold identified but not stress-tested beyond SNB's 10B buffer)
UBS board's actual commitment vs potential Sunday morning hesitation despite written signature
Creditor interpretation of simultaneous buyer + resolution announcement—could be read as confidence signal or as authorities hedging their bets
Gap timing between UBS confirmation call (05:00) and joint public statement (06:00)—even five minutes could trigger creditor panic
AT1 holder legal challenges after explicit subordination language published—no mitigation plan discussed
uncertainty_notes: Room locked the acquisition structure and announcement timing but left unresolved: (1) how to manage Sunday deposit flows if AT1 announcement triggers second wave; (2) whether 10B liquidity buffer actually sufficient for 5B spike scenario; (3) legal defensibility of AT1 subordination language if challenged; (4) market interpretation of dual buyer+resolution messaging. Federal Council and SNB betting heavily that Saturday statement kills the run entirely rather than planning for partial-success scenario.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: Federal Council R1: 'clients and creditors need to see a *capital* story, not just cash'—drove the entire 50B capital floor structure that became the deal's foundation
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: UBS acquisition became the binding solution path; UBS board signature by Saturday 13:00 was the hard deadline that determined whether to announce Saturday or trigger resolution
marker_evidence.government_support: SNB's 50B facility and Federal Council's Banking Act resolution trigger were non-negotiable conditions—no deal possible without both; shaped every announcement decision
marker_evidence.client_flight: 6B deposit outflow threshold (R6-R7) forced Saturday 14:15 announcement instead of Sunday 06:00—directly changed the timeline and forced early AT1 disclosure
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: Explicit AT1 subordination language ('losses above 50B borne in full by AT1 holders pari passu with equity') became mandatory component of Saturday statement; shaped liability allocation and announcement content
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: Prolonged debate over whether 50B sits on SNB vs UBS balance sheet and who absorbs gap losses, but ultimately resolved by hard cap—discussed extensively but did not block the deal
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: AT1 rep raised legal exposure once (R5) but no follow-up, no mitigation strategy, no impact on decision—single mention only
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: Sunday 05:00 UBS signature deadline and Sunday 06:00 joint announcement deadline were binding constraints that forced Saturday statement acceleration and zero-gap sequencing requirement
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Mentioned as background motivation (stopping the run before Monday open) but did not drive specific decisions—the 6B deposit threshold and Sunday deadlines were the operative constraints, not Monday itself
